title: Content
description: The content interface: octets to document and back, for one or more content types. This is the entire content of the rule that the kernel knows nothing about JSON — a shape applies to what a content component decoded, never to a guess (shape spec §2.2). See spec.md §6.

document.description: The decoded document, in the shape language's value model (shape spec §2.1) — JSON values plus bytes. The shape applies to this.

encoded.description: How to read 'document'. Absent means the natural JSON value; 'base64' means octets, for content that decodes to a byte string rather than to structure.

degradations.description: Value-dependent distinctions this decode could not preserve, each with the path where the loss occurred (spec.md §6.4). Static ones are declared in the handshake instead.

Encode.title: Encode
Encode.description: Decode's inverse, and how a selected variant's document becomes the octets a mock serves. decode(encode(d)) must equal d (spec.md §6.2).

shape.description: The slot's shape document, owned by design 2.2.

path.description: Where in the plan the returned fragment is spliced.

fragment.description: A plan fragment in design 2.4's grammar, using core actions and this component's own namespaced actions and nothing else. Returning nothing is legitimate: the kernel then compiles the slot generically and calls decode at execution time (spec.md §6.3).

grammar-version.description: The plan-grammar version the fragment was authored against. An engine whose grammar has moved on either accepts it or fails naming the skew; it never silently reinterprets (spec.md §12.3).

Detect.title: Detect
Detect.description: Do these octets look like a type you handle? For the shape language's content-type operator, the one operator that inspects octets (shape spec §4.2). Optional; used to resolve an absent content type, never to override a declared one (spec.md §6.5).
